message.text: The change puts `evidence.budget`, a size limit on this clone's evidence directory, into `MelianConfig`. The check run's request key hashes `decisive(input.config)`, which is the whole configuration minus only `output` and `publish.emoji`. So the evidence budget is now an input to every check run's key, but no check reads it and it can never change what a check finds.

/** `budget`: the bytes the clone's evidence directory may hold before a write is refused. */
	readonly evidence: { readonly budget: number };

The key leaves these out, each for its reason:

- `output` and `publish.emoji`, which change how a review reads and never what a check finds.
- The preference file's path and Stryker's install path, which name the host. What the preference file says reaches the key through the configuration.

- **Something is in it that should not be.** The key never matches, so work reruns, or a dismissal stops applying. A boundary nonce does this on every run. So did the round's overrides inside a verdict's policy fingerprint, which kept a dismissal from re-deciding its round.

| Check request, producer `check`, and `identityKey` | `pipeline/src/check-request.ts`, `pipeline/src/checks.ts` | reuses a completed or running check run of the tier and starts none | Display-only configuration, `output` and `publish.emoji`. The preference file's path and Stryker's install path, which name the host; the configuration holds what the preference file says. `PATH`, `HOME` and `TMPDIR`, which name the host and which no bounded fact stands for. A test under mutation can turn on each, so a mutation run is reused only on the host that ran it. A record shared across hosts carries one for the round that read it, and no other host attaches a run to it, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-15. On one host, a shell with another `PATH`, `HOME` or `TMPDIR` can still reuse a mutation run made under different values; [issue #458](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/458) would close `HOME` and `TMPDIR`, and leave `PATH` deciding which `git` and `sh` a test spawns. `LANG` when mutation is off, since Biome and tsc store no tool text, by [the decision of 2026-11-15](../decisions/2026-11-15-check-run-keys-lang-under-mutation.md). A task resumed after a crash runs on the host facts and install its new process has, all but `LANG`, which its input carries, and records under the first key, until [issue #459](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/459). The request holds the policy source, Melian's tool pins, and each analyser's version and source. It holds a digest of each lockfile and each package manager's install records from `installDigests`, `unavailable` for one that is missing and `unreadable` for one that cannot be read, and whether those identify the install. With mutation on, it holds Stryker's facts, the head's trust, the cold flag and the tools' `LANG`. It also holds `code`, the checks' code version, `codeVersion("checks")`, a digest of the recorded hash of every module TypeScript lists as reached from `checks.ts`, which the gate ties to the source by [the decision of 2026-11- [cut at 2 KiB]

explanation.what: The change puts `evidence.budget`, a size limit on this clone's evidence directory, into `MelianConfig`. The check run's request key hashes `decisive(input.config)`, which is the whole configuration minus only `output` and `publish.emoji`. So the evidence budget is now an input to every check run's key, but no check reads it and it can never change what a check finds.
explanation.whatToDo: Leave `evidence` out of the check request: destructure it away in `decisive` in `check-request.ts`, next to `output`, with a one-line comment giving the reason. Add `config.evidence` to the `excluded` list in `check-request.test.ts`. Update the check-request row in `docs/guidelines/identity.md` and the exclusion list in the request-keys decision to name it. Alternatively, keep the clone-local budget out of `MelianConfig` and load it separately from the configuration that reviews read.
explanation.whyHere: The request-keys decision (base, "What a check run's key holds and leaves out") keys the configuration less the keys that "change how a review reads and never what a check finds". The identity guideline names "Something is in it that should not be. The key never matches, so work reruns" as a way a key goes wrong. Its check-request row lists `output` and `publish.emoji` as the only configuration left out. `evidence.budget` falls under that reason: it bounds a directory that only `compare adjudicate` writes. The change keeps the decision's shape ("configuration less display keys") and breaks its reason. It also did not update the check-request row, which the guideline says a change to a key must do in the same commit. The cost is real because the change's own refusal message and doctor warning tell the user to raise `evidence.budget`, which is exactly the edit that throws away every reusable check run.

properties.failureScenario: A maintainer runs `melian review main...feature` with feature checked out, so policy is read from the working tree with preferences. The static check run completes and is stored under key K. They adjudicate a valid miss and get the change's refusal: "Raise evidence.budget in your configuration until the prune lands in issue #627". They do that by adding `evidence:\n  budget: 4GiB` to `melian.local.yaml`, or to `~/.config/melian/config.yaml`. `loadConfig` merges it into `config.evidence`. `runIdentity` in `checks.ts` passes `config: input.config` to `checkRequest`, and `decisive` keeps `evidence`, so the key becomes K' ≠ K. The next `melian review main...feature` of the same base and head finds no run under K'. Guardrails, Biome, tsc, Enola and, when it is enabled, the mutation check all run again from scratch, and the old run is never reused. With the budget in the user-level `config.yaml`, this happens once for every range review on every repository on that machine. The same split happens across hosts: a clone that set its own budget and a host on the 1 GiB default key the same check request differently, so their check records never share the slot that the check-record key is meant to share "whichever host ran it". No check result changes in any of these cases.
